one_line: US export controls and memory shortages disrupt global AI supply chains, while regulators target governance, data privacy, and hardware policies worldwide.

themes.title: US export controls and hardware shortages
themes.text: New US export controls have halted AI server shipments to four Southeast Asian nations and stalled billions in data center loans tied to Chinese firms. Meanwhile, memory shortages have extended delivery times for Nvidia chips, and Chinese labs like Z.ai faced launch delays due to computing restrictions.

themes.title: Data privacy and chatbot toy bans
themes.text: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general asked a bankruptcy court to block Character.ai's auction of private chat data. Separately, New York banned AI chatbot toys for five years, and cybersecurity researchers discovered that confidential user data sent to MiniMax was accessed by unknown parties.

themes.title: Satellite deployment and hacker AI tools
themes.text: The FCC authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million Starmind satellite data centers by 2040. Microsoft reported that state-backed hackers from China and North Korea integrated the AI penetration testing tool Artex into their workflows.
